quotes.text: Generative artificial intelligence isn’t a trend; it’s the backbone of the next industrial era. Countries around the globe are racing to build the full AI stack: data centers, chips, power, and platforms. Here in the United States, we must ensure that we have the right policies in place to have enough energy to power AI and make America an attractive place to build the entire AI supply chain.

America’s adversaries are not waiting for us to figure this out. If AI can find serious vulnerabilities in widely used software, China and other bad actors will look for ways to use similar tools against us. We need to make sure trusted American defenders have the coordination, access, and support required to stay ahead.

There is no one-size-fits-all approach to regulating this technology, nor should there be. To unlock the full potential of AI, we must establish foundational protection for the data that powers many of these new AI tools by enacting a comprehensive data privacy standard in the United States.
In the same way humans are not perfect, AI is not perfect, either. Because humans design AI algorithms, AI systems may contain unintentional bias, which unfortunately could lead to discrimination.

we are talking about all the AI, and one of the things—of course, we have had a lot of questions about, in the past, about how algorithms are set, especially when we are talking about AI. How would you make sure that those algorithms are correct, that they are not biased to one side or the other?

I want to be an AI contrarian because I think it can do tremendous things for communications. That if we introduce machine learning and pattern recognition on our wired and wireless networks, we are going to be able to radically increase our efficiency.

This legislation will require the Consumer Product Safety Commission to establish a pilot program to explore the use of artificial intelligence in support of its product safety efforts.

Mr. Speaker, I move to suspend the rules and pass the bill (H.R. 1770) to direct the Consumer Product Safety Commission to establish a pilot program to explore the use of artificial intelligence in support of the mission of the Commission and to direct the Secretary of Commerce and the Federal Trade Commission to study and report on the use of blockchain technology and tokens, respectively.

We are in an AI race with Communist China, and America cannot afford to let foreign adversaries influence decisions involving our data center infrastructure. The @HouseCommerce Committee is working to address this challenge because the United States must lead the future of AI, not follow it.

The @HouseCommerce Committee passed the Ratepayer Protection Act during today’s full committee markup!

This legislation protects American ratepayers from being forced to cover the cost of energy infrastructure upgrades needed to support data centers. I was proud to support this bill as we strengthen America's leadership in the AI race against Communist China while ensuring local communities aren't left footing the bill.

Protecting the American people means ensuring the systems they rely on every day, including our hospitals, water systems, and electric grid, remain safe, secure, and reliable. Our adversaries are constantly looking for new ways to target our critical infrastructure, and we must make sure we are prepared to respond.

I enjoyed speaking with @HansNichols this morning at the Axios Electricity in Transition event. We discussed the importance of passing the Ratepayer Protection Act, the current landscape surrounding artificial intelligence, and the need to secure our electricity supply chains and streamline energy infrastructure permitting. Our full conversation: https://t.co/9WS4emrAcI
